newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall slightly, horizontal trend seen.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall slightly, horizontal trend seen.

text.p: Polish shares fell slightly in lower turnover on Thursday and analysts said they were likely to swing within a narrow band next week as the market was waiting for clear signals to give it direction.
The WIG index fell 94.4 points, or 0.6 percent, to 14,631.7 and turnover fell 6.6 percent to 101.2 million zlotys ($36.1 million) on both markets as 47 issues fell, 12 rose and 19 were flat.
"It might inch up tomorrow on the back of today's strong buying after price fixing, but next week is likely to be flat or just down," said Adam Drozdowski, an analyst at BGZ house.

Analysts said the strong technical resistance at the September 18, 30-month high of 14,832.7 points of the WIG index and the proximity of the psychological barrier of 15,000 points were halting investors' buying mood.

They said press reports that the central bank president suggested interest rates might be raised to avoid a banking crisis after the recent boom in credit action was unlikely to influence the market significantly.

"I believe this (the statement) should be understood that one shouldn't expect a rate cut in the next six months, but I don't think there would be a rate-raise," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Polska.
Analysts said the market could stay in the horizontal trend until mid-October when companies' earnings reports for September are due.
Continuous trade turnover amounted to 1.6 million zlotys ($0.6 million) with the biggest mover Stalexport falling 1.4 percent.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 2.5 percent in a 34.6-million-zloty ($12.4 million) turnover in the regular session and rose 3.8 percent in 27.4-million-zloty (9.8 million) continuous trade.
